title: Halden Review Lamp - Pull-Cord Theme Toggle with Radial Reveal

affordance_translation.physical_behavior: A brass reading lamp hung from the ceiling: tug the beaded pull cord a short distance with springy resistance; the bulb lights and pools amber glow under the shade.
affordance_translation.digital_mechanic: The theme toggle is a hanging lamp button: clicking tugs the cord 14px with a spring, then the new theme spreads from the bulb as a growing clip-path circle (640ms) on the View Transitions root snapshot instead of a global fade. Night mode lights the bulb, pools glow, and shifts accents rust to lamp-yellow. The circle origin is measured from the bulb's actual bounding box at click time, so the reveal is always anchored correctly at any viewport.

design_tokens.borders: Editorial hairlines (masthead rules); lamp drawn as SVG line work with a shade path, collar, bulb circle
design_tokens.elevation: Glow ellipse and pooled light under the shade as the only depth cues
design_tokens.typography: Serif headline with one italic word, rust drop cap, newspaper-style masthead (volume/number, evening edition)

interactive_mechanics: Cord tug spring animation on click; Enter/Space perform the same pull for keyboard users
Radial clip-path circle theme reveal originating at the bulb (View Transitions API)
Fallbacks: 400ms crossfade for browsers without View Transitions and for prefers-reduced-motion
aria-pressed state with label describing the RESULT of the next press
usability_notes: The accessibility spec is the reason to keep this entry: button semantics, result-oriented aria-label, keyboard-equivalent pull, motion fallbacks - while the physics stays purely visual (SVG aria-hidden). Copy this pattern's discipline wherever a physical control replaces a settings toggle. Source: design-lounge.live component writeup with full behavior spec.
